facts.text: I need help to write an article about a contract clause in the NSW HIA Lump Sum contract.
I provided an extract of clause 17 of the NSW HIA Lump Sum contract and asked the assistant to remember it.

Clause 17.1 requires the owner to pay the deposit stated in Item 2(b) of Schedule 1 on the later of the day the contract is signed by the owner and the day warranty insurance described in Schedule 6 is in force and the owner is provided with a certificate of insurance.
The deposit is brought to account with the first progress payment.
Clause 17.2 requires the owner to pay the contract price progressively as claimed by the Builder.
Clause 17.3 requires the builder to give the owner a written claim for a progress payment for the completion of each stage.

Clause 17.4 requires a progress claim to state the amount claimed and not paid for the stage completed, the amount claimed and not paid for contract price adjustments, the amount claimed and not paid for variations, and the sum of those amounts.
Clause 17.5 requires the owner to pay a progress claim within 5 working days of the builder giving the claim.
Clause 17.5 states that payment of a progress claim is on account only and the owner has no right of set off.
Clause 17.6 states that other than in relation to the final progress claim, payment of a progress claim is on account only and the owner has no right of set off.
The NSW HIA Lump Sum contract is subject to the Home Building Act 1989 (NSW).
I provided an extract of Section 8A of the Home Building Act 1989 (NSW) about maximum progress payments (other than small jobs).

Section 8A(2) authorises progress payments only if they are one of the following kinds: a specified amount or percentage payable following completion of a specified stage described in clear and plain language; or a progress payment for labour and materials in respect of work already performed or costs already incurred supported by invoices, receipts or other reasonably necessary documents with payment intervals fixed by the contract or on an 'as invoiced' basis; or a progress payment authorised by the regulations.
Section 8A(4) prohibits demanding or receiving payment of an unauthorised progress payment and entering into a contract entitling a person to demand or receive an unauthorised progress payment.
Section 8A(4) sets a maximum penalty of 1,000 penalty units for a corporation and 200 penalty units for any other case.
Section 8A(5) states that Section 8A does not apply to a progress payment under a construction contract to which the Building and Construction Industry Security of Payment Act 1999 applies.

Section 8A(6) provides exceptions where Section 8A does not apply, including contracts between parties who each hold a contractor licence for work authorised by their contractor licence, and contracts for specialist work that is not also residential building work.
I provided Clause 35 (Dispute Resolution) of the NSW HIA Lump Sum contract and asked the assistant to acknowledge it.
Clause 35.1 requires that if a dispute arises, a party must give written notice to the other party setting out the matter in dispute.
Clause 35.2 requires the builder and the owner to meet within 10 working days of giving the notice to attempt to resolve the dispute or agree on methods of so doing.
Clause 35.3 requires that if the dispute is resolved, the parties must write down the resolution and sign it.
Clause 35.4 states that anything done or said in the negotiation cannot be revealed in any other proceeding.
The NSW HIA Lump Sum contract is subject to Section 13 of the Building and Construction Industry Security of Payment Act 1999 (NSW).
I provided an extract of Section 13 of the Building and Construction Industry Security of Payment Act 1999 (NSW) about payment claims.

Section 13(1A) allows a payment claim to be served on and from the last day of the named month in which the construction work was first carried out (or related goods and services were first supplied) and on and from the last day of each subsequent named month.
Section 13(1B) allows an earlier date for serving a payment claim if the construction contract makes provision for an earlier date in a particular named month.
Section 13(1C) allows a payment claim to be served on and from the date of termination for a construction contract that has been terminated.
Section 13(2) requires a payment claim to identify the construction work (or related goods and services), indicate the amount claimed, and state that it is made under the Act.

Section 13(4) allows a payment claim to be served only within the period determined by or in accordance with the terms of the construction contract or within 12 months after the construction work last carried out (or related goods and services last supplied), whichever is later.

Section 13(5) provides that, except as otherwise provided for in the construction contract, a claimant may only serve one payment claim in any particular named month for construction work carried out or undertaken to be carried out (or related goods and services supplied or undertaken to be supplied) in that month.

Section 13(6) states that subsection (5) does not prevent serving a single payment claim in respect of more than one progress payment, including an amount that has been the subject of a previous claim, or serving a payment claim in a particular named month for construction work in a previous named month.
Section 13(7) states that a head contractor must not serve a payment claim on the principal unless the claim is accompanied by a supporting statement indicating that it relates to that payment claim.

keyphrases: payment on account only no set off
maximum progress payments other than small jobs
Building and Construction Industry Security of Payment Act 1999 NSW Section 13 payment claims
